issues.reason: The whenever machinery keys the response on the trigger occurrence, and a dependent existential must be "a Skolem function of every universal that scopes over it", so (sk_reset $a) collapses every failure of that apprentice's lanterns into one and the same reset event asserted During each distinct failure — a falsehood the per-occurrence key would avoid.

defect_summary: Key the response on the trigger: (Member (sk_reset $e) reset) (Patient (sk_reset $e) (sk_solo_count $a)) (During (sk_reset $e) $e) — or (sk_reset $e $a) as a function of both universals — while the count itself correctly stays (sk_solo_count $a).
notes: Everything else conforms: the indefinite participants route bare "when P, Q" to the whenever rule, both genitives take Possession (neither a lantern nor a count is part of a person), solo_count gets its genus with the non-predicable modifier unexposed, and fail/reset take Patient as change-of-state undergoers.
